items.title: Emile Barnes Interview, 1962-01-03
items.q: Say you were playing with him and he got pretty far off the melody.

ctx.x: They had no more melody. Clarinet played more melody than that? Yeah. Most of the clarinet played. It was leading. Well, about when would you say the clarinets started to play something besides the main melody? When did they get off? When did the trumpet take the melody? When did that begin?

Well, the trumpet and clarinet was partly the same. They kept partly the same melody. The more the tone was different. You see, but the clarinet would get off more than the trumpet would get off. See, the trumpet was a whole melody, but the clarinet would get off and violate. Now, you see, you take a man, a person like Freddie Kaepernick, you know, you're very careful. Well, if he can't, to a certain distance, I didn't get away from it. He got away altogether. You want to watch the melody with him. That's the way…
Say you were playing with him and he got pretty far off the melody. What would you do on clarinet then?
